newsitem.title: GERMANY: Shell hopes for $1.5 bln invest in Ukraine energy.
newsitem.headline: Shell hopes for $1.5 bln invest in Ukraine energy.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell International Gas hopes to invest up to $1.5 billion in oil and gas ventures in Ukraine, a company executive told an investment conference on Tuesday.

Business Development West Director Alex Kulpecz said the company was seeking a 20 percent share in the former Soviet republic's existing gas transit pipelines, which bring Russian fuel supplies to countries west of Ukraine.

He said Shell's potential investment, previously put by Ukrainian officials at $1 billion, would be "$1.5 billion, in part 20 percent of the existing pipeline structure. We all know there is major potential in Ukraine."
He said Shell would look to form a joint venture with Ukraine in which the company would hold 49 percent.
Shell has been negotiating with Kiev for at least a year on investment deals, which, if realised, would equal the country's total foreign investment since independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
Royal Dutch/Shell won a tender late last year to explore four blocks on Ukraine's Black Sea shelf and a joint venture is to be formed with Ukraine's Chornomornaftogaz to drill for oil there.
